items.title: Society of Authors to form AI focus group to work on new charter
items.excerpt: The Society of Authors is forming an AI focus group to draft a new charter, after its earlier 'Ethical AI Charter' sparked member backlash and was retracted.

items.title: 'Keep it human': James McAvoy describes using AI for audio as 'food without calories'
items.excerpt: British Audio Award-winning narrator James McAvoy (JD Kirk's Recall, Audible Originals) urged the audiobook industry to reject AI narration, calling it 'food without calories'.

items.title: IPG partners with London Book Fair on AI training event
items.excerpt: The Independent Publishers Guild and London Book Fair will run a half-day training event on using AI in publishing, covering workflow opportunities and copyright-protection challenges.

items.title: "우리 아이가 동화책 주인공으로"…AI로 만드는 맞춤 동화
items.excerpt: 하얀꿈ENM이 아이의 일상 사연을 공모받아 AI로 맞춤형 동화책을 제작한다. 첫 체험 10가족을 선정했고, 그림책 기반 영상·오프라인 체험으로 확장을 검토 중이다.

items.title: AI의 저작물 학습, 어디까지 허용…26일 표준계약서 공청회
items.excerpt: 문화체육관광부가 한국저작권위원회·법무법인 세종과 함께 26일 'AI 학습용 저작물 이용허락 표준계약서(안)' 공청회를 연다. 출판물 등 저작물을 AI 학습에 쓸 때의 이용·양도 기준을 담았다.

items.title: NVIDIA Seeded Pirated Books and Shared Them With Adobe, Authors Allege
items.excerpt: Book authors' amended complaint accuses NVIDIA of seeding pirated books via BitTorrent after downloading them from Anna's Archive and LibGen for AI training, and of sharing them with partners including Adobe.
items.note: off-list (allowed_domains had no fresh item on this authors-v-AI-training case)

items.title: "Not a win – but it is not a dead loss": Industry responds to Joint Select Committee on AI report
items.excerpt: Australia's Joint Select Committee on AI recommended strengthening copyright, but the APA and ASA say the report does not rule out an 'opt-out' approach to AI training on books.

items.title: Getbackers Voice Comic Staff Apologizes for Generative AI Use in PR Video
items.excerpt: Staff of the GetBackers manga voice-comic reboot apologized for using generative AI in a promotional video, while insisting the voice comic itself does not use generative AI.

items.title: Les industries culturelles ouvrent une consultation citoyenne sur l'IA
items.excerpt: Eleven French cultural-industry bodies including the SNE publishers' union, the writers' CPE and Sofia launch a Make.org citizen consultation on AI and human creation, running 23 Nov 2026 to 17 Jan 2027.

items.title: Fan art, mangas et IA : France et Japon face à l'avenir de la création
items.excerpt: Part of ActuaLitté's Japan reportage: how French and Japanese manga publishers and creators handle fan art, piracy and generative AI as threats to authorship.

items.title: "Corriger le texte d'une machine et traduire une œuvre sont deux gestes différents"
items.excerpt: Rafael Patron of the Italian association of translation professionals argues for verifiable commitments, not just principles, as AI enters literary translation: post-editing machine output is not translating.

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: The American Literary Translators Association's amicus brief in the authors' suit against OpenAI and Microsoft argues AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model output'.

items.title: New analysis finds no evidence of racial bias in Pangram
items.excerpt: A new analysis finds no evidence that cultural differences in writing style make the AI detector Pangram return false positives, though it doesn't rule out bias in how accusations are made; follow-up to the Esquire debate.

items.title: Just-in-Time Synthesis: A New Approach to an Old Genre
items.excerpt: Compares a commissioned review article with an AI-generated just-in-time overview answering the same reader need, asking how each is made and whether a reader can tell the difference.

items.title: The Anatomy of 'Harm': An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses the federation's study detailing the harm generative AI causes publishers and authors, and what collective licensing can do about it.

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Analysis of the Third Circuit's Sept. 29 ruling that ROSS's unlicensed copying of Westlaw headnotes to train an AI legal-search tool was not fair use; argues the more an AI is marketed as solving research tasks, the less transformative it is for STM content, and that an emerging AI-licensing market weighs against fair use.

items.title: [윤주혜의 C] 투고 쏟아지고 문학상 응모 최다…AI가 불붙인 '딸깍 출판'
items.excerpt: AI가 써준 200쪽 원고와 돈만 있으면 책을 낼 수 있는 '딸깍 출판' 시대 — 출판사 투고와 문학상 응모가 역대 최다로 몰리며 출판계가 AI 원고 판별에 부담을 겪고 있다는 칼럼. (11-18 ajunews AI 원고 급증 카드의 후속/칼럼이라 중복 가능성 있음.)

items.title: Can an Indie Author Make a Whole Cozy Mystery Series Look From an Image Model? My Cover Tests
items.excerpt: Hands-on test of making a consistent three-book cozy-mystery cover series, audiobook square and thumbnails with an image model (Nano Banana Pro API, book 1 as reference), with costs vs $400-900 commissioned covers and a disclosure/ethics section. Caution: names a specific API; check for advertorial tone.

items.title: 한국저작권위원회-국립중앙도서관, AI 시대 도서관 사서 대상 저작권 교육 실시
items.excerpt: 한국저작권위원회와 국립중앙도서관이 전국 도서관 사서 41명을 대상으로 '인공지능 시대, 도서관에서 알아야 할 저작권 및 활용사례' 교육을 20일 진행했다.

items.title: Not AI's to Take survey data suggests weakening copyright could lose votes
items.excerpt: The Not AI's to Take campaign released a survey of 1,464 voters finding that weakening Australia's copyright laws for AI training would cost votes in 21 key electorates. (Body paywalled; excerpt from feed.)

items.title: "AI Drafts, Humans Refine": HiveMind Launches Aurorah Translation Supporters Program
items.excerpt: HiveMind, operator of Aurorah, which combines LLM translation with human post-editing to cut costs while preserving cultural nuance, launched a translation supporters program for Korean content.
